question_text: What is the primary purpose of a CPU?
correct_answer: Execute instructions and process data

question_text: Which component of a CPU performs arithmetic and logical operations?
correct_answer: ALU

question_text: What is the purpose of CPU registers?
options: Provide fast temporary storage inside the CPU
Connect the CPU to the internet
correct_answer: Provide fast temporary storage inside the CPU

question_text: What does the Program Counter (PC) normally contain?
options: The address of the next instruction
correct_answer: The address of the next instruction

question_text: What does the Instruction Register (IR) hold?
options: The address of the next program
correct_answer: The instruction currently being processed

question_text: What is the main role of the CPU control unit?
options: Generate control signals that coordinate CPU operations
correct_answer: Generate control signals that coordinate CPU operations

question_text: Which sequence best represents the basic instruction cycle?
correct_answer: Fetch, decode, execute

question_text: What is a datapath in a CPU?
options: The collection of components that manipulate and transfer data
correct_answer: The collection of components that manipulate and transfer data

question_text: What does ISA stand for?
correct_answer: Instruction Set Architecture

question_text: What does the CPU clock provide?
options: Timing signals that synchronize processor operations
correct_answer: Timing signals that synchronize processor operations

question_text: Which component temporarily stores operands and results during CPU execution?
correct_answer: Registers

question_text: Which part of an instruction specifies the operation to be performed?
correct_answer: Opcode

question_text: Which bus carries data between CPU components and memory?
correct_answer: Data bus

question_text: Which architecture separates instruction memory and data memory?
correct_answer: Harvard architecture

question_text: In a basic Von Neumann architecture, instructions and data are stored in:
correct_answer: The same memory system

question_text: In a single-cycle CPU, an instruction is completed in:
correct_answer: One clock cycle

question_text: What is a control signal used for in a CPU datapath?
options: Select or enable specific hardware operations
correct_answer: Select or enable specific hardware operations

question_text: Why are multiplexers commonly used in CPU datapaths?
options: To select one of multiple possible data inputs
correct_answer: To select one of multiple possible data inputs

question_text: What is a register file?
options: A collection of CPU registers that can be accessed by instructions
A file stored on a hard drive
correct_answer: A collection of CPU registers that can be accessed by instructions

question_text: Which operation is typically performed by an ALU?
options: Instruction fetching from an external network
correct_answer: Addition

question_text: Which type of control unit generates control signals using combinational logic?
correct_answer: Hardwired control unit

question_text: What is a key characteristic of a microprogrammed control unit?
options: Control signals are generated using microinstructions
correct_answer: Control signals are generated using microinstructions

question_text: What is the purpose of a sign extender in a CPU?
options: Extend a smaller signed value to a larger width while preserving its value
correct_answer: Extend a smaller signed value to a larger width while preserving its value

question_text: What is the purpose of an instruction decoder?
options: Interpret the opcode and generate or assist in generating appropriate control signals
correct_answer: Interpret the opcode and generate or assist in generating appropriate control signals

question_text: What is the main benefit of instruction pipelining?
options: Increase instruction throughput by overlapping execution stages
Make every instruction execute in zero time
correct_answer: Increase instruction throughput by overlapping execution stages

question_text: What does CPI represent in processor performance analysis?
correct_answer: Average clock cycles per instruction

question_text: Which factor directly affects CPU execution time according to the basic CPU performance equation?
options: Instruction count, CPI, and clock cycle time
correct_answer: Instruction count, CPI, and clock cycle time

question_text: What is the main difference between RISC and CISC instruction sets?
options: RISC generally uses simpler instructions, while CISC generally supports more complex instructions
correct_answer: RISC generally uses simpler instructions, while CISC generally supports more complex instructions

question_text: Which hazard occurs when two pipeline stages require the same hardware resource at the same time?
correct_answer: Structural hazard

question_text: What is a pipeline stall?
options: A delay inserted into the pipeline to resolve a condition that prevents normal execution
correct_answer: A delay inserted into the pipeline to resolve a condition that prevents normal execution

question_text: Which pipeline hazard occurs when the outcome of a branch determines which instruction should be fetched next?
correct_answer: Control hazard

question_text: Which dependency is a Read After Write (RAW) hazard?
options: An instruction reads a value before an earlier instruction has written it
An instruction writes a value before reading it
Two instructions write the same value simultaneously
correct_answer: An instruction reads a value before an earlier instruction has written it

question_text: What is forwarding used for in a pipelined CPU?
options: Send a computed result directly to a dependent instruction without waiting for normal register write-back
correct_answer: Send a computed result directly to a dependent instruction without waiting for normal register write-back

question_text: What is the purpose of branch prediction?
options: Predict branch behavior so instruction fetching can continue with fewer control stalls
correct_answer: Predict branch behavior so instruction fetching can continue with fewer control stalls

question_text: What characterizes a superscalar processor?
options: It can issue multiple instructions in a clock cycle using multiple execution resources
It executes exactly one instruction every clock cycle
correct_answer: It can issue multiple instructions in a clock cycle using multiple execution resources

question_text: What is out-of-order execution?
options: Executing independent instructions when their operands and resources are ready rather than strictly following program order
Executing instructions only in reverse order
Running instructions without a control unit
correct_answer: Executing independent instructions when their operands and resources are ready rather than strictly following program order

question_text: Why is cache memory important in CPU design?
options: It reduces average memory access latency by keeping frequently needed data closer to the CPU
It permanently stores all user files
It eliminates the need for registers
correct_answer: It reduces average memory access latency by keeping frequently needed data closer to the CPU

question_text: What is the primary role of an MMU in a modern CPU?
options: Translate virtual addresses to physical addresses and enforce memory protection
correct_answer: Translate virtual addresses to physical addresses and enforce memory protection

question_text: What is the primary purpose of register renaming in an out-of-order CPU?
options: Reduce false dependencies caused by reuse of architectural registers
correct_answer: Reduce false dependencies caused by reuse of architectural registers

question_text: What is a critical path in a synchronous CPU circuit?
options: The longest combinational path that limits the minimum clock period
The path used to boot the operating system
The route between CPU and internet
The path used to store files
correct_answer: The longest combinational path that limits the minimum clock period

question_text: What is clock skew in a synchronous digital system?
options: A difference in the arrival time of a clock signal at different circuit elements
A difference between two instruction opcodes
correct_answer: A difference in the arrival time of a clock signal at different circuit elements
